abstract: This paper presents the results of laboratory tests analysing the effect of accelerated thermal ageing on the temporal characteristics of polarisation and depolarisation currents, of transformer insulation samples made of NOMEX®910 hybrid cellulose-aramid electrical insulating paper, impregnated with Nytro®BIO 300X insulating liquid. The accelerated laboratory thermal ageing process consisted of annealing samples of the analysed insulation, at a number of selected temperatures, over a specified period of time. The temperatures and annealing times of the samples were chosen to replicate as closely as possible the ageing process of transformer insulation occurring during the long-term operation of power transformers in the structure of the National Power System. To determine the degree of ageing of the samples tested in the laboratory, the polarisation and depolarisation current analysis method (PDC Method) was used. The result of the analysis are regression functions of the activation energy and dominant time constants of the components of the cellulose-aramid insulation NOMEX®910, with consideration of the effect of temperature and the degree of thermal degradation of the cellulose fibres.

articleTitle: Extreme Weather Effects on Transmission Grids and the Potential of the Utilization of Real Time Monitoring for Smart Grids Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Extreme weather events are increasing and becoming more frequent because of global warming and hence the exposure of transmission lines can have detrimental effects on our modern power systems. The power systems and especially transmission lines were designed for expected weather conditions and the rapid change in weather is putting a real strain on the transmission line grid. The transmission lines have not changed fundamentally in the last 100 years, and they have not been considered when it comes to advancements in technology over the last few decades. There are no common practices in monitoring transmission lines, but recent advancement has finally made real time monitoring a financially reasonable decision. This paper will review different extreme weather events and how they can affect transmission lines and how the real time monitoring of these effects could be utilized for smart grid applications in transmission grids.

articleTitle: Survey on LED lamps for residential applications: characterization of performance
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Aim of the paper is to conduct a survey of the present market, focusing on the best-selling retrofit LED lamps and to analyze experimentally their fundamental EMC performance for subsequent classification of the LED drivers. Two stage experimental characterization testing approach is adopted. First, input current and output luminous flux in steady-state under nominal supply conditions is acquired. Next, transfer of input supply voltage interharmonics to output visible flicker components in terms of gain factor curves is obtained. Based on the achieved and discussed testing results, classification of the LED lamps is developed.

articleTitle: Providing Intelligent Maintenance through an Autonomous Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article focuses on trends in the field of intelligent maintenance in a utility company. One of the main goals of every transmission and distribution (T&D) system operator is reliable performance of their network with low interruption time. To achieve this goal, fully functional and healthy components are required. During their lifetime after installation and commissioning, components age and gradually change from new to old. Aging in this sense means continuous deterioration of their operability or resilience against normal and abnormal voltage and current stresses. This deterioration may lead to equipment failure if maintenance is not performed early enough. The article shows how automation can be used for remote management and maintenance of assets at an electrical substation.

articleTitle: Modelling and Testing Transformer Differential Protection in Inverter-Based Generation Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of inverter-based power generation, the evaluation of network protection performance and coordination of protection systems deserves closer examination. The electrical protection of power transformers with fault contribution from electronic interfaced power sources imposes new application challenges that have to be dealt with by protection engineers. Even though transformer differential protection has been successfully employed as the main protection of power transformers for many years due to its simple principle of ampere-turn balance and first Kirchhoff’s law, one of the major challenges to its successful application is the discrimination of fault currents from inrush currents due to transformer energization and overexcitation. In the case of an electronic-based power interface, the current waveform and harmonics content (2<sup>nd</sup>, 3<sup>rd</sup>, 5<sup>th</sup>) in the fault currents may significantly impact the inrush stabilizing algorithm used in conventional transformer differential protection. The advanced transformer protection may use the current waveform analysis (CWA) algorithm to discriminate internal faults from inrush. The CWA algorithm is able to detect internal faults just after the first cycle after fault inception and block the standard second harmonic inrush stabilization. The investigated power system is a large-speed drive with an active front end in a four-quadrant rectifier that can be operated in motor and generator mode. The active front end is a modular multilevel converter with LVRT capability. For a detailed analysis of the transients, the modular multilevel converter is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink with an adequate control strategy. The transformer is modelled with nonlinear characteristic. The MATLAB/Simulink environment tests included external faults, internal faults at the grid and converter side and turn-to-turn faults. Selected cases are shown and discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Testing of Airport Runway Lighting Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Nowadays, in demanding conditions of the 4<sup>th</sup> industrial revolution optimization of materials, manufacturing processes and production cost are come more and more to the fore. Paper provides an insight into the topic of cables for lighting airport runways. After summarizing the most important insulation materials used in medium-voltage airport cables, their general electrical parameters are described. Five samples produced with different technologies and design specifications were subjected to a non-destructive partial discharge measurement test, and the sample with best results was tested in the scope of electrical type test.

articleTitle: Evaluation IEC 61850 Protocols based Protection Schemes of Digital Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Although IEC 61850 GOOSE and Sampled values (SVs) have demonstrated to be highly reliable for use in multiple applications, many users still experience fears and challenges with the actual transition to digital substation based on IEC 61850 communication protocols. Therefore, more experimental studies and research are needed to encourage the deployment of digital stations rather than traditional ones. This paper aims to evaluate IEC 61850 technique for digital substation in comparison to conventional methodology. This paper describes in detail how IEC 61850 GOOSE and SV can be implemented for protection schemes as part of the continuing efforts to digitize stations. The work outlines the hardware & software implemented and analyses the laboratory testing results.
